text:
ashley: heads up — we just saw a huge spike in pod connection drops on westus2-gpu during the nightly model migration. apps doing cross-AZ RPCs started failing readiness.
raj: which symptoms? packetloss, conntrack logs, or kube-proxy errors? :thinking:
maria: prometheus alert fired for conntrack_utilization > 90% on gpupool-westus2 :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Alert: ALERT ConntrackHighUsage (instance=gpupool-westus2-nodegroup) fired at 2032099980
ashley: logs look like this on a bunch of nodes:

"nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet (node 10.0.4.17)"
"kube-proxy: conntrack: failed to create entry"

ashley: quick checks I ran:
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count -> 65536
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max -> 65536
ss -tan | wc -l -> 120k (many in TIME_WAIT)

raj: ok that matches conntrack saturation. Can you also dump conntrack entries to see top tuples? `conntrack -L | awk '{print $5}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head`
maria: also check ip_local_port_range, we sometimes hit small ephemeral range during bulk outbound. `cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`
ashley: ip_local_port_range = "32768 60999"
ashley: ran `conntrack -L | tail -n 5` and we're seeing lots of 10.0.x ephemeral src ports from kube-proxy SNAT on pods being torn down.
raj: immediate mitigation options:
- reduce migration concurrency (cut the job parallelism in half)
- temporarily bump nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes
- widen ip_local_port_range to free more ephemeral ports
- consider short-term NAT-sweeper daemon to remove stale entries for terminating pods

maria: can you bump now and see if it stabilizes? also record exact nodes so we can patch cloud-init later.
ashley: doing a live bump on node 10.0.4.17 now:

# sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
# sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 65535"
# echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max

ashley: after bump, conntrack_count -> 91234 (down from ~65536 + churn) — traffic resumed for most pods, readiness flaps stopped.
raj: good. We need durable fixes though. Short-term patchlist:
- rollout sysctl changes via node bootstrap and daemonset (persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-redwood.conf)
- add conntrack usage alert at 70% with `for: 5m` so we don't get surprised
- add a pre-migration gating check to ensure avg(conntrack_utilization) < 50% before starting bulk migration

maria: long-term:
- increase nf_conntrack_buckets appropriately at kernel boot (so table resize is efficient)
- reduce NAT reliance where possible for east-west: enable `kube-proxy` endpoint slice/DSRR options if available, or move certain intra-cluster traffic to ClusterIP (avoid SNAT)
- investigate RDMA paths/MTU mismatch causing more connections per job (we saw some retransmit spikes)

ashley: noted transient RDMA/MTU hints — during the migration we had a mix of jumbo-frame and non-jumbo hosts (mtu 9000 vs 1500) in the same overlay, causing bursty retransmits and extra conntrack churn.
raj: action: schedule a zone-aligned migration (keep migration traffic within same AZ) and add an MTU-compliance check in the migration playbook.

infra-bot: Created task INF-3241: "Persist conntrack sysctl + pre-migration gating" assigned to ashley
maria: also propose a small daemonset that runs `conntrack -L --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED` pruning entries older than X seconds for pods in Completed/Terminating state — doc needed for safety review.
ashley: I'll draft the runbook and post to eng-infra. Immediate: I'll keep the bumped sysctl for next 24h and watch alerts. Will also throttle the rest of migration batch for 2 hours.
raj: follow-ups for next week:
- kernel bump on gpupool images to support larger bucket counts
- update cloud request for more ephemeral ports quota if provider limits apply
- postmortem with timeline + cost impact (extra egress from retries)
maria: leaving a note: alert noise reduction and precise metrics (conntrack_count / nf_conntrack_max) should be visible on per-node dashboards.
ashley: thanks all. I'll update the thread when migration completes or if we see reoccurrence. :thumbsup:
